From Cassie to Digit 5: Agility Robotics’ path to workplace robots

Agility’s robot generations trace a shift from bipedal locomotion research to practical warehouse work, safety and production readiness.

The Robot Report ↗16 September 2026English editorial summary
StoryImages 2Videos 5

From walking research to useful work

Agility Robotics began with Cassie, which took its first steps in 2016 and focused on bipedal movement. The first Digit followed in 2017 for researchers. The development path reflects a shift from walking performance to tasks that businesses need done.

Digit reaches commercial applications

Digit 3 in 2019 targeted package delivery and box handling, with a lifting capacity of about 18 kilograms. Ford bought the first two robots to explore deliveries from a vehicle to a doorstep. Digit 4, introduced in 2023, focused on warehouses and distribution centres.

Workplace lessons inform Digit 5

The fifth generation changes the leg structure to favour force over speed and updates the battery and systems for operating near people. According to Agility, the robot assesses risk and slows down or stops when a person approaches.

Company scale and plans

The report describes a workforce of more than 400 and a factory capable of producing up to 10,000 robots per year. That figure is capacity, not actual deliveries. It also discusses a proposed SPAC transaction that had not been completed at the time of reporting.
